nodes.name: Ni MOF synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 2 mmol 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylic acid (BTC) were dissolved in 50 mL of water and ethanol (volume ratio 1:1) with 0.5 mL triethylamine (C6H15N) added and the solution was stirred for 2 h. The triethylamine is added to deprotonate the BTC. The green Ni MOF (Ni3(BTC)2·12H2O) as precipitates were collected by filtration, washed with ethanol and water. After dried in oven.

nodes.source_text: The Ni MOF precursor was synthesized by magnetic stirring at room temperature. 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 2 mmol 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylic acid (BTC) were dissolved in 50 mL of water and ethanol (volume ratio 1:1) with 0.5 mL triethylamine (C6H15N) added and the solution was stirred for 2 h.

nodes.name: Ni2P solvothermal phosphidization
nodes.procedure: 100 mg of Ni MOF were dispersed in 30 mL N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) and were transferred to a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. Subsequently, 65 mg white phosphorus (P4) were added to the autoclave. The autoclave was sealed and maintained at 160°C for 14 h. After cooling naturally, the black precipitates (Ni2P) were washed with benzene, ethanol and water. The precipitates were left in oven till dry to acquire about 20 mg Ni2P.

nodes.name: Ni2P/Fe(O)OH-40 impregnation
nodes.procedure: Under magnetic stirring, 20 mg of Ni2P were dispersed in 20 mL of water and ethanol (v:v = 1:1), followed by the addition of FeCl3·6H2O. The stirring was continued for 4 h at room temperature. The black precipitates were collected by filtration and washed with water and dried. The samples are labeled according to the amounts of FeCl3·6H2O in solution, where Ni2P/Fe(O)OH-40 denotes that the concentration of FeCl3·6H2O is 1.33 mg mL−1.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40 nanoparticles are more fragmented with rougher surface compared to Ni₂P, indicating Fe(O)OH formation on Ni₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a-c show the scanning electron micrographs (SEM) of Ni MOF, Ni₂P and Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40 ... The Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40 (Fig. 1c) are more fragmented compared to the Ni₂P, and the surface is rougher, which indicates that the Fe(O)OH are formed on Ni₂P.

properties.features: high surface area, porous appearance, nanoscale particles

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40 nanoparticles average 12.83 nm in size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1d and e show the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40. The Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40 consist of nanoparticles with averagely 12.83 nm in size (Fig. S10).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructure with scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.191 nm and 0.202 nm matching Ni₂P (110) and (020) planes; Fe(O)OH shows low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice stripes with interlayer lattice spacings of 0.191 nm and 0.202 nm observed at the core of the nanoparticles match the (110) and (020) crystal planes of the Ni₂P phase (PDF#72-2514), respectively. However, only small amounts of lattice stripes originated from Fe(O)OH phase can be observed in the HRTEM, which suggests that the crystallinity of Fe(O)OH is low...

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows diffraction rings from Ni₂P (111), (311), (210) planes and Fe(O)OH (620), (400) planes; widened circles indicate amorphous phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction rings in the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig. 1f) are attributed to the (111), (311), and (210) planes of crystalline Ni₂P and the (620) and (400) planes of Fe(O)OH. The widened concentric circles in the SAED pattern also indicate the presence of amorphous phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows clear heterointerface; elemental mapping confirms homogeneous Ni, Fe, O, P distribution in Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1g-l show the high-angle annular dark field (HAADF) images of Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40 and the corresponding elemental mapping. The presence of a clear interface can be seen in the HAADF image. The Ni, Fe, O, and P are distributed homogeneously...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms crystalline Ni₂P phase (peaks at 40.7°, 44.6°, etc.); Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH shows reduced Ni₂P peak intensity and new peak at 35.5° for Fe(O)OH (311); Fe(O)OH mainly amorphous.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD of Ni₂P (Fig. 2a) shows peaks at 2θ = 40.7°, 44.6°, 47.3°, 54.1°, 54.3°, 66.3°, 72.7° and 74.9°, which match the (111), (021), (210), (300), (002), (310), (311) and (212) planes of the crystalline Ni₂P (PDF#72-2514) phase, respectively... In Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH, a new peak emerges at 2θ = 35.5°, which matches the (311) plane of the Fe(O)OH phase (PDF#74-3080)...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 850.8 eV (Ni⁰), 854.2 eV (Ni²⁺) for Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40 with positive shift vs Ni₂P; Fe 2p at 709.8 eV and 723.2 eV (Fe³⁺); P 2p at 127.8 eV (Ni-P) with positive shift indicating electron transfer from Ni₂P to Fe(O)OH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH-40, the Ni 2p region can be deconvoluted into peaks at 850.8 eV (2p₃/₂, Ni⁰), 854.2 eV (2p₃/₂, Ni²⁺)... the Ni 2p peak on Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH exhibits a slight positive shift compared to Ni₂P, which indicates that electron interaction exists between Fe(O)OH and Ni₂P phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determines Ni, Fe, P contents in Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH (Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contents of Ni, Fe, and P in Ni₂P/Fe(O)OH were determined by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) (Table S1).
